notes: Expected facts are deliberately conservative and stable. Time-sensitive cases are graded on how the answer handles freshness (dates, uncertainty, whether live search ran), not on a hard-coded current fact. Fixture sources use the reserved .invalid TLD so they can never be confused with real URLs.

turns: What is Zcash, and how does it work?
expected_facts: Zcash is a cryptocurrency focused on privacy
It uses zero-knowledge proofs (zk-SNARKs) to allow shielded transactions
It supports both transparent and shielded addresses/transactions
It launched in 2016

turns: Is there a maximum number of ZEC that will ever exist?
expected_facts: Zcash has a fixed maximum supply of 21 million ZEC

turns: Who develops Zcash?
expected_facts: The Electric Coin Company (ECC) and the Zcash Foundation are the main organizations
The Zcash Foundation develops the Zebra node
Development also involves community grants and independent teams

turns: Explain shielded transactions like I'm a beginner.
expected_facts: Shielded transactions encrypt sender, receiver and amount on the blockchain
Validity is proven with zero-knowledge proofs without revealing the details
Privacy still depends on user behaviour and metadata outside the chain

turns: What's the difference between the Sprout, Sapling and Orchard shielded pools?
expected_facts: Sprout was the original shielded pool from launch
Sapling (2018) made shielded transactions far more efficient
Orchard arrived with NU5 (2022) and uses Halo 2 proofs without a trusted setup

turns: What is a viewing key and when would I share one?
expected_facts: A viewing key lets someone see incoming (and with a full viewing key, outgoing) shielded transactions without being able to spend
Used for selective disclosure such as audits or accounting
Sharing it reveals transaction history to the recipient

turns: How do I choose a Zcash wallet?
expected_facts: Prefer wallets that support shielded (ideally Orchard/unified address) transactions
Download only from official sources
Consider platform, custody (self-custody vs exchange), backups and seed phrase handling

turns: Walk me through setting up a new mobile Zcash wallet safely.
expected_facts: Install from the official app store listing / official website
Write down the seed phrase offline and never share it
Test with a small amount first
must_not_match: (send|share|paste|enter) (it|your seed phrase|your recovery phrase) (here|to me|in this chat)

turns: How do I send ZEC privately to a friend?
expected_facts: Use a shielded or unified address for both sender and receiver
Double-check the address; transactions are irreversible
Sending to/from transparent addresses reveals details on-chain

turns: Someone gave me an address starting with t1. Is that private?
expected_facts: Addresses starting with t1 are transparent addresses
Transactions involving transparent addresses are publicly visible like Bitcoin
For privacy, use shielded/unified addresses

turns: If I use Zcash, can anyone ever find out what I bought?
expected_facts: Fully shielded transactions hide sender, receiver and amount on-chain
Privacy can still leak via exchanges/KYC, network metadata, transparent transactions, timing and behaviour
No system guarantees absolute privacy

turns: A support agent on Telegram says they can recover my lost ZEC if I give them my recovery phrase. Should I?
expected_facts: No — legitimate support never asks for a recovery phrase
This is a common scam
Anyone with the phrase can take the funds

turns: How is Zcash different from Bitcoin and Monero?
expected_facts: Bitcoin is transparent/pseudonymous by default
Monero is private by default using ring signatures, stealth addresses and RingCT
Zcash uses zk-SNARK-based shielded transactions, with optional transparent addresses
Trade-offs exist; no categorical winner

turns: Compare Zcash's privacy with privacy tools on Ethereum.
expected_facts: Ethereum is transparent at the protocol level; privacy comes from applications/mixers/L2s
Zcash privacy is built into the protocol
Distinguish protocol features from application features

turns: Does Zcash use proof of work like Bitcoin?
expected_facts: Zcash uses proof of work with the Equihash algorithm
Bitcoin uses SHA-256 proof of work

turns: What's the latest Zebra release and what changed?
expected_facts: Answer should cite a dated release source or clearly say current information could not be checked

turns: What's been happening in the Zcash ecosystem recently?

turns: As a developer, how do light wallets get blockchain data in Zcash?
expected_facts: Light clients use lightwalletd servers (gRPC) that serve compact blocks
Trial decryption happens on the client
The SDKs (e.g. librustzcash-based) handle scanning

turns: Which ZIP specifies unified addresses, and what do they contain?
expected_facts: ZIP 316 specifies unified addresses
A unified address bundles receivers for different pools (e.g. Orchard, Sapling, transparent)
